[P2] Distinguish clock resets from event-loop stalls

A regression exceeding one second does not necessarily mean the test environment reset. A synchronous step can block the main thread's fake-clock advancement while the worker continues running and timestamps a callback timeout. The next request then reports a client time more than one second behind that timeout. This condition accepts the regression, allowing subsequent history events—and even execution completion—to precede the callback's recorded end. Keep timestamps monotonic within a clock generation and permit backward movement only on an explicit reset signal. Add coverage for a regression exceeding one second without an environment reset.
